label: Gaza City
sub: Major population center; heavily bombarded in Oct 2023 – Mar 2025 IDF operations. Pre-war population ~700,000.

label: Rafah
sub: Southern Gaza city at Egyptian border; IDF major ground operation began May 2024. ~1.4M displaced persons sheltering at peak.

label: Khan Yunis
sub: Second-largest Gaza city; major IDF ground operation Dec 2023 – Apr 2024. Yahya Sinwar's home city.

label: Jabaliya Refugee Camp
sub: Largest refugee camp in Gaza (pop. ~110,000). Site of First Intifada outbreak 1987. Repeatedly struck by IDF 2023-2025.

label: Al-Shifa Hospital
sub: Gaza's largest hospital. IDF raided Nov 2023 and Mar 2024 claiming Hamas command infrastructure. WHO reported hospital rendered non-functional.

label: Kerem Shalom / Karem Abu Salem
sub: Main commercial crossing between Israel and Gaza for goods. Repeatedly closed during military operations; targeted by Hamas mortar fire.

label: Rafah Border Crossing
sub: Only Gaza crossing not controlled by Israel; connects to Egypt. Closed by Israel after Oct 7 seizure of Philadelphi Corridor. Sole evacuation route for many civilians.

label: Erez / Beit Hanoun Crossing
sub: Northern Gaza pedestrian crossing. Attacked and destroyed by Hamas on Oct 7, 2023. Basis for proposed aid port in northern Gaza. Reopened on May 1, 2026 following US diplomatic pressure — first reopening in months.

label: Kibbutz Kfar Aza
sub: One of the hardest-hit Israeli communities on Oct 7; 64 residents killed, many homes destroyed. Remains uninhabited as of 2026.

label: Kibbutz Be'eri
sub: 108 residents killed on Oct 7 — deadliest Oct 7 site for a single community. Hamas also murdered hostages during IDF response.

label: Nova Music Festival Site
sub: 364 attendees massacred by Hamas gunmen on Oct 7. Site near Kibbutz Re'im. Memorial erected; site visited by world leaders.

label: Jerusalem — Old City
sub: Contains Temple Mount/Haram al-Sharif (holy to Jews and Muslims), Western Wall, Church of Holy Sepulchre. Sovereignty disputed; both Israel and Palestine claim capital status.

label: Temple Mount / Haram al-Sharif
sub: Most contested religious site. Administered by Jordanian Waqf since 1967. Ben-Gvir provocations in 2026: April 12 (third incursion), April 22 (526 settlers stormed compound on Independence Day), May 14 (Jerusalem Day — Ben-Gvir raised Israeli flag next to Dome of the Rock, MK Kroizer called for demolishing mosques and building Third Temple; Jordan condemned as 'dangerous provocation'). Ben-Gvir's May 14 visit was his fifth documented 2026 storming of the compound.

label: Ramallah — PA Headquarters
sub: De facto administrative capital of the Palestinian Authority. Muqata'a compound — PA Presidential offices, Arafat's tomb. In Area A (full PA control).

label: Hebron (Al-Khalil) — H2
sub: Divided city: H1 (PA) and H2 (Israeli military control, ~500 settlers among 30,000 Palestinians). Most contested West Bank flashpoint. Cave of the Patriarchs / Ibrahimi Mosque.

label: Jenin Refugee Camp
sub: Northern West Bank refugee camp; IDF Operation Defensive Shield 2002 killed dozens. Continued IDF counterterrorism raids 2023-2026. Stronghold of armed Palestinian factions.

label: Nablus
sub: Major West Bank city; frequent site of IDF raids. Home of Al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades, Lion's Den faction. On May 3, 2026, IDF conducted an overnight raid in the Old City market killing one Palestinian and wounding three others. Rising West Bank violence 2022-2026.

label: Ma'ale Adumim
sub: Largest Israeli settlement in the West Bank (~40,000 residents). Located just east of Jerusalem, effectively bisects Palestinian West Bank. Subject of US warnings against annexation.

label: Ariel
sub: Major settlement in central West Bank (~20,000 residents), 20km east of Green Line. Location is a key obstacle to territorial contiguity in two-state proposals.

label: Gush Etzion
sub: Settlement bloc south of Jerusalem (~80,000 residents across multiple settlements). Jewish presence pre-1948; often cited in Israeli positions as core settlement area.

label: Qalandia Checkpoint
sub: Main checkpoint between Ramallah and Jerusalem. Symbol of West Bank movement restrictions; 20,000+ Palestinians cross daily for work. Site of frequent confrontations.

label: Bethlehem
sub: Birthplace of Jesus; Palestinian city in Area A. Church of the Nativity. Separation barrier surrounds city on three sides, cutting it from Jerusalem. Economy dependent on Christian pilgrimage tourism.

label: Jericho
sub: Oldest continuously inhabited city in the world. First Palestinian city transferred to PA control under Oslo. In Area A; surrounded by Area C.

label: Deir el-Balah
sub: Central Gaza city; major UNRWA facilities. Became one of the largest displacement centers during 2023-2025 war. UN World Food Programme distribution hub.

label: Sheikh Jarrah
sub: East Jerusalem neighborhood; Israeli court-ordered evictions of Palestinian families sparked the May 2021 crisis and Operation Guardian of the Walls. Focal point of settler land claims.

label: Sderot
sub: Israeli city 1.5km from Gaza border; under constant rocket fire since 2001. Thousands of rockets have struck or landed near the city. Population partially evacuated Oct 2023.

label: Ashkelon
sub: Israeli coastal city; major target of Hamas rockets including on Oct 7. Contains power plant that historically supplied Gaza. Population ~155,000. On May 3, 2026, flotilla activists Saif Abu Keshek (Spanish-Palestinian) and Thiago Ávila (Brazilian) appeared before an Israeli court here alleging torture; detention extended. May 20–21, 2026: Israeli activist Zohar Regev and dozens of the 87 detained Global Sumud Fleet activists were processed through Ashkelon Magistrate's Court; National Security Minister Ben-Gvir posted a viral video showing activists cable-tied and kneeling, triggering 14+ countries to summon Israeli ambassadors, an Italian EU sanctions request, and Poland's intent to ban Ben-Gvir from entry.

label: UNRWA Gaza Operations
sub: UNRWA operates 279 schools, 22 health centers in Gaza. HQ area in Gaza City damaged. Over 200 UNRWA staff killed since Oct 7. Israel accused UNRWA of Hamas ties; US suspended then partially restored funding.

label: Tulkarm
sub: Northern West Bank city; Nur Shams and Tulkarm refugee camps. Major IDF counterterrorism operations 2023-2025; site of sustained militant activity.

label: Beit Lahiya / Beit Hanoun
sub: Northern Gaza towns; among most heavily bombarded areas in 2023 war. Virtually entirely destroyed; remained under IDF control through 2025.

label: Haifa
sub: Israel's third-largest city; major port and technology hub. Struck by Hezbollah rockets during Lebanon conflict parallel to Gaza war (2024).

label: Philadelphi Corridor
sub: Narrow strip along Gaza-Egypt border; key smuggling route for Hamas weapons. Israeli military occupation of corridor was major ceasefire sticking point. IDF says tunnels ran beneath.

label: Jalud & Qaryut Villages
sub: Palestinian villages south of Nablus. Attacked by ~100 masked settlers March 22, 2026 (10+ homes torched, village council burned). Again on April 28, 2026, settlers burned a Palestinian family home and beat an elderly man while IDF soldiers stood by; 12 settlers involved, only 1 arrested. Repeated targeting makes Jalud a focal point of West Bank settler violence in 2026.

label: Silwan — Batn al-Hawa
sub: East Jerusalem neighborhood where 11 Palestinian families were forcibly evicted March 25, 2026 via Ateret Cohanim settler organization. ~90 families (700 people) at risk. Courts apply 1970 Israeli law with no reciprocal Palestinian property-return right.

label: Mukhmas
sub: West Bank village northeast of Jerusalem. Palestinian-American teenager Nasrallah Abu Siyam shot and killed by Israeli settlers on March 27, 2026 — second Palestinian-American killed by settlers in under a year.

label: Eshtaol — Iranian Missile Strike
sub: Jerusalem-area town struck by Iranian ballistic missile on March 28, 2026. Air defense failed to intercept; 11 lightly injured; extensive property and structural damage in 150-meter radius. IAF launched investigation into defensive failure.

label: Bani Suheila — IDF Strike Zone
sub: Area east of Khan Younis, adjacent to the Gaza ceasefire buffer zone. Site of IDF drone strike on March 28, 2026 targeting Hamas-linked vehicle; 1 killed, several wounded.

label: Tiberias
sub: Northern Israeli city on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee. Targeted by Hezbollah rocket fire on March 29, 2026 as part of coordinated multi-front attack alongside Iranian missile salvos; sirens sounded across the Galilee region.

label: Dheisheh Refugee Camp
sub: Palestinian refugee camp south of Bethlehem; established 1949 for 1948 Nakba refugees. Frequent site of IDF raids. A 15-year-old Palestinian boy was shot and killed by IDF during a March 30, 2026 military raid during a 'violent riot.'

label: WHO Vehicle Attack — Southern Gaza
sub: Israeli forces fired on a clearly marked WHO humanitarian vehicle in southern Gaza on April 6, 2026, killing one person. Incident raises serious concerns under international humanitarian law regarding protection of medical and aid workers.

label: Maghazi Refugee Camp
sub: Refugee camp in central Gaza. Site of April 7, 2026 Israeli airstrikes that killed at least 10 Palestinians after an Israeli-backed militia attempted to abduct Hamas Qassam Brigade members. Clashes between the militia and camp residents preceded the strikes.

label: Ne'ot Hovav (Ramat Hovav)
sub: Chemical industrial zone 12km south of Beersheba; Israel's most concentrated hazardous chemical manufacturing area. Struck by Iranian ballistic missile on March 29, 2026, evading air defense; hazmat emergency protocols activated with area evacuation ordered.

label: Mansoura Water Filling Station
sub: The only operational truck filling point for the Mekorot water supply line serving Gaza City. Struck by Israeli fire on April 17, 2026, killing two UNICEF-contracted water truck drivers. UNICEF suspended all contractor operations following the attack. Supplies water to hundreds of thousands of Gazans.

label: Majd al-Ba'a — Settler Arson Zone
sub: Area west of Yatta, south of Hebron, where Israeli settlers from the Otniel settlement torched two Palestinian vehicles on April 17, 2026. Part of ongoing settler violence surge in southern West Bank documented by OHCHR and B'Tselem.

label: Turmus Ayya — Settler Raid
sub: Central West Bank town near Ramallah. Raided by ~20 armed and masked settlers on April 18, 2026, who torched buildings, vandalized property, and spray-painted 'Revenge' in Hebrew. IDF later raided homes in the village but made no settler arrests.

label: al-Mughayyir — Settler School Attack
sub: Palestinian village northeast of Ramallah. On April 21, 2026, Israeli settlers attacked al-Mughayyir Boys School, killing 14-year-old student Aws Hamdi al-Na'san and 32-year-old Jihad Marzouq Abu Na'im. One of the deadliest single-day settler attacks of 2026; village has been repeatedly targeted by settlers from nearby outposts.

label: West Bank IDF Raids
sub: Israeli army conducted overnight raids across the occupied West Bank on April 12, 2026, continuing sustained military operations in the territory. Source: Al Jazeera.

label: Deir Dibwan — Settler Shooting
sub: Palestinian village east of Ramallah. On April 22, 2026, Israeli settlers shot and killed one Palestinian and injured others. Israeli forces detained approximately 30 people during the incident. Occurred one day after the deadly settler attack on al-Mughayyir school (April 21), part of an intensifying wave of settler violence during Israel's Independence Day period.

label: Duma Village — Settler Raid
sub: Palestinian village in the central West Bank, 11km southeast of Nablus. Known internationally as the site where the Dawabsheh family was burned alive by Israeli settlers in July 2015 (18-month-old baby killed). On April 25, 2026, settlers raided the village and an adjacent Bedouin hamlet, injuring a woman and a child in the latest wave of settler violence following the April 21–23 killings.

label: Sheikh Radwan — Election Day Strike Zone
sub: Neighborhood in western Gaza City. On April 25, 2026, Israeli forces struck near a Hamas police station in Sheikh Radwan while Hamas officers were deployed for election-day security during Gaza's first municipal elections in 20 years. A 14-year-old teenager also died on April 26 from injuries sustained in an earlier strike in this neighborhood.

label: Tayasir — Settler Shooting (Apr 2026)
sub: Palestinian village east of Tubas in the northern Jordan Valley. Alaa Khaled Sabih (28) was shot and killed by armed Israeli settlers during an attack on the village in April 2026 — part of the surge in settler violence documented by Save the Children, which found 685 Palestinian children displaced by settler attacks in January–March 2026 (10x the prior quarterly average).

label: Silwan al-Bustan — Mass Displacement Risk
sub: East Jerusalem neighborhood facing what UN officials describe as 'one of the largest expulsion waves since 1967.' Accelerated Israeli demolition orders in April 2026 threaten displacement of 2,000+ Palestinians. Israel approved 34 new settler outposts in a classified Cabinet vote April 1, 2026 — largest single-step recognition of unauthorized settlements in Israeli history.

label: al-Mawasi Coastal Strip
sub: Narrow coastal strip along southern Gaza's Mediterranean coast, between Khan Younis and Rafah. Designated by Israel as a 'humanitarian zone' during the 2023–25 war; repeatedly struck despite designation. Major displacement camp site for hundreds of thousands of Gazans. On May 6, 2026, IDF drone strike killed Hamas anti-narcotics police colonel Naseem al-Kalazani near al-Mawasi, wounding 17 others.

label: Sa-Nur (Sanur) Settlement
sub: Re-established Israeli settlement in northern West Bank near Jenin, originally evacuated under Israel's 2005 Gaza disengagement plan. On May 9, 2026, settlers demanded a Palestinian family in adjacent Al-Asasa village exhume and rebury their 80-year-old father within 30 minutes from a cemetery 300 meters from the settlement. Israeli soldiers present did not intervene. The UN Human Rights Office described the incident as an example of 'growing dehumanization' of Palestinians. One of several re-established settlements in the northern West Bank since 2023.

label: Jaljilya Village
sub: Palestinian village near Ramallah in the West Bank. On May 13, 2026, Israeli settlers entered Jaljilya searching for stolen sheep; a riot broke out as they departed, leading IDF and Border Police to open live fire, killing one Palestinian. Incident typifies ongoing settler-triggered confrontations across the West Bank, which UN figures show resulted in 122 Palestinian deaths in April 2026 alone.

label: Jordan River Border — IDF 'Sulfur and Fire' Drill
sub: Location of IDF 'Sulfur and Fire' snap readiness drill on May 15, 2026, observed by IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir with the 96th and 80th regional divisions plus special forces. Zamir cited the Oct 7 attack as evidence of the need for constant border readiness. Drill reflects ongoing Israel-Jordan tensions over Israeli settler actions and Ben-Gvir's Temple Mount incursions.

label: Muslim Quarter — Jerusalem Day Flag March
sub: Route of the annual Jerusalem Day Flag March through the Muslim Quarter of the Old City, held on May 15, 2026. Tens of thousands of ultranationalist marchers chanted 'Death to Arabs' and 'May your village burn'; 13 arrested; Ben-Gvir stormed Al-Aqsa; Palestinian shops shuttered. Jordan condemned the march as a 'dangerous provocation that inflames religious sentiments.'

label: Rimal — IDF Strike Zone (May 2026)
sub: Upscale residential neighborhood in western Gaza City. On May 15, 2026, Israeli forces struck an apartment building and nearby vehicle in Rimal, killing Hamas armed wing chief Izz al-Din al-Haddad — one of the last surviving architects of Oct 7 — along with 6 others; 50+ wounded. Additional IDF strikes on Rimal residential buildings reported May 16. Area also struck April 28, 2026 (senior Hamas intelligence operative killed).

label: ICC — Israel Arrest Warrant Proceedings
sub: ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I issued arrest warrants for PM Netanyahu and former Def. Min. Gallant in November 2024. May 13, 2026: ICC Appeals Chamber rejected Israel's jurisdictional challenge 3-2; Israel abandoned formal defense. May 19, 2026: Smotrich confirmed ICC prosecutor sought warrant against him — charges include apartheid (potentially first-ever ICC apartheid warrant), forced displacement, persecution, and transfer of civilian population. This is represented symbolically on the map; the ICC is located in The Hague, Netherlands.

label: Khan al-Ahmar (E1 Corridor)
sub: Bedouin Palestinian community (~250 residents) in the strategic E1 corridor east of Jerusalem, between Jerusalem and Ma'ale Adumim settlement. Demolition halted by Israeli High Court in 2018 after international protests. May 19, 2026: Finance Minister Smotrich ordered immediate evacuation and demolition — framed as retaliation for ICC warrant application. May 25, 2026: UN Special Coordinator Mladenov warned demolition would constitute 'a defiant war crime'; EU High Representative Kallas and Jordan's Foreign Ministry intensified opposition. E1 location makes Khan al-Ahmar critical to geographic contiguity of a Palestinian state.

label: at-Tawam — Police Post Strike (May 23)
sub: Area in northern Gaza near the ceasefire buffer zone. On May 23, 2026, Israeli forces fired two missiles at a Hamas police post here, killing five police officers and a 13-year-old civilian boy, wounding 10+ (1 critical). Hamas condemned the strike as deliberate targeting of civil governance to 'create a security vacuum' ahead of Board of Peace disarmament talks.

label: Nuseirat Refugee Camp
sub: One of the eight original Palestinian refugee camps established in central Gaza after the 1948 Nakba. Extremely densely populated. On May 24, 2026, an Israeli airstrike struck an apartment building here killing a family of three — Mohammad Abu Mallouh, Alaa Zaqlan, and their 6-month-old infant son Osama — with ~10 more wounded. Bodies transferred to Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir el-Balah.

label: Kiryat Shmona
sub: Northern Israeli city ~3 km from the Lebanese border; frequent target of Hezbollah rocket fire. On May 30, 2026, Hezbollah fired 2 rockets at Kiryat Shmona — both intercepted by Israeli air defense. Bennett and Lapid publicly called for a 'powerful response' to Hezbollah attacks. Site of ongoing cross-border fire throughout the Gaza ceasefire period.

label: Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital — Deir al-Balah
sub: One of Gaza's few partially functional hospitals in central Gaza; major trauma and surgery center. On May 30, 2026, an Israeli drone strike near the hospital killed Dr. Jamal Abu Aoun, head of the anaesthesia department at Al-Yafa Medical Hospital — adding to the 1,000+ healthcare workers killed in Gaza since October 2023. WHO has documented 700+ attacks on health facilities since October 7, 2023.

label: Idhna — Settler Attack (June 5, 2026)
sub: Palestinian village in Hebron governorate, southern West Bank. On June 5, 2026, Israeli settlers attacked the village: one Palestinian was beaten and injured, a second was wounded by IDF gunfire when troops arrived at the scene, and settlers set fire to Palestinian-owned agricultural fields. Idhna attack is part of the ongoing pattern of settler violence across the West Bank documented throughout 2026.

label: Tel Rumeida — 7-Month-Old Baby Killed (June 6, 2026)
sub: Area in H2 Hebron under Israeli military control. On June 6, 2026, IDF soldiers fired on a vehicle, killing 7-month-old Sam Fahd Abu Haikal and wounding both parents. IDF's initial inquiry found the family were uninvolved civilians. International condemnation followed. H2 Hebron is home to ~500 Israeli settlers among 30,000 Palestinians and is a recurring flashpoint for IDF use of force.

label: Huwara — Settler Rampage + IDF Soldier Joining Beatings (June 6, 2026)
sub: Palestinian town south of Nablus on Route 60. On June 6, 2026, settlers attacked Huwara, wounding 9 Palestinians. Surveillance video captured an IDF soldier in full military gear beating two Palestinian men alongside settlers — a documented instance of IDF troops joining settler violence rather than restraining it. The IDF called the actions 'serious and inconsistent with IDF values.' Huwara was the site of a major settler rampage in February 2023 and has remained a focal point of settler violence.

label: Nuseirat — Funeral Procession Strike (July 17, 2026)
sub: Israeli drone struck mourners outside the Ahmad Yassin Mosque during a funeral procession, killing 8 and wounding 20. Israel claimed the gathering included an Islamic Jihad cell, without public substantiation. Part of a wave that killed 14 across Gaza that day.

label: At-Tawani — Mosque, Homes, Dairy Factory Burned (July 19, 2026)
sub: Israeli settlers set fire to the village mosque, two Palestinian homes, and a dairy factory in at-Tawani, Masafer Yatta, South Hebron Hills. Part of the surge that made July 2026 (with March) the deadliest month for settler-violence deaths since October 2023.

label: Tal Village — Shootout Near Havat Gilad (July 24, 2026)
sub: A settler raid on the village of Tal, southwest of Nablus, sparked a confrontation in which a Palestinian seized a weapon from a settler in apparent self-defense, killing him, before Israeli forces killed the Palestinian and three more died in the ensuing shootout. Two Israeli soldiers were also killed. Israel launched a wide-scale West Bank operation in response.

label: Qusra — Rahma Mosque Torched (July 26, 2026)
sub: Israeli settlers set fire to the Rahma Mosque in Qusra, south of Nablus, vandalizing it with graffiti reading 'Benayahu's Revenge' and Stars of David, amid an IDF wide-scale West Bank operation following the July 24 Tal village shootout.

label: Qusra — Settler Siege of 3 Families (Aug 9–13, 2026)
sub: Extremist settlers besieged three Palestinian families in their homes in Qusra, cutting water and electricity, in what residents called an attempt to seize their land. IDF launched a 3-day operation to clear settler outposts but the families remained unable to fully return home as of Aug 13.

label: Ganim — Settlement Officially Reopened (Aug 13, 2026)
sub: Israel held an official reopening ceremony for the Ganim settlement near Jenin, 21 years after its 2005 evacuation under the Sharon disengagement plan. Defense Minister Israel Katz attended; ~24 prefab homes already installed.

label: Beit Lahia — Tuk-Tuk Strike (Aug 12, 2026)
sub: Israeli drone strike killed municipal worker Mohanad Saada and wounded 5 near the Western Roundabout in Beit Lahia — Israel's first Gaza strike in over a week. IDF said it targeted a Hamas commander; Gaza Civil Defence disputed this.

label: Khan Younis — Motorcycle Strike (Aug 13, 2026)
sub: Israeli drone strike on a motorcycle in the al-Amal neighborhood killed Huthaifa Kawari and critically wounded another; IDF claimed, without evidence, he commanded a Hamas unit.

label: Gaza City — Police Colonel Killed (Aug 13, 2026)
sub: Drone fired three missiles at a vehicle on al-Rashid Street in Sheikh Ajleen, killing Gaza civil police chief Col. Jamal Abu Kamil, 43. Gaza's Interior Ministry called it an assassination; IDF alleged a Hamas commander role without evidence.

label: Sa'ir — Settler Shooting (Aug 14, 2026)
sub: Roughly 30 settlers from a nearby outpost attacked the al-Uddeissa area of Sa'ir, shooting nurse Muhammad al-Mutawwar, 26, in the back — severing his spine and leaving him permanently paralyzed. A second woman was also shot.

label: Qusra — Siege Continues, IDF Fails to Clear Settlers (Aug 15, 2026)
sub: More than a dozen settlers again arrived at the besieged Palestinian home; IDF dispatched troops but made no arrests and settlers departed only voluntarily. UN and Palestinian Foreign Ministry condemned the ongoing six-day siege.

label: Al-Eizariya — Wedding Hall Raid (Aug 15, 2026)
sub: Israeli forces stormed a wedding hall, firing sound bombs and using pepper spray on attendees before arresting several guests, including the groom.

label: Burqa — Settlers Beat, Pepper-Spray Three Palestinians (Aug 16, 2026)
sub: Settlers from a nearby pastoral outpost assaulted three Palestinians in al-Masoudiya, beating them, spraying them with pepper spray, and damaging their vehicle. Same night, settlers separately raided al-Mughayyir and Sinjil near Ramallah.

label: Beit Imrin — Settler Siege, IDF Arrests All Nine Trapped Occupants (Aug 16, 2026)
sub: Settlers besieged a home for over three hours, blocking residents and Red Crescent ambulances. IDF then raided the house itself, arresting all nine occupants and confiscating Red Crescent ambulance keys.

label: Umm Safa — New Illegal Outpost Tents Pitched (Aug 16, 2026)
sub: Settlers pitched tents in the Wadi Zeytun area near Umm Safa, northwest of Ramallah, in an attempt to establish a new illegal outpost.

label: Qusra — UN Delivers Aid, Siege Eases but Continues Into Second Week (Aug 17, 2026)
sub: UN teams delivered water, food, medicine and hygiene kits to the besieged families; municipal workers restored water/power. IDF removed the settlers' tent but erected its own in the same spot, continuing the closure.

label: Beit Imrin — Second Raid, Two Injured (Aug 18, 2026)
sub: Israeli soldiers assaulted two Palestinians during a fresh raid on Beit Imrin, two days after the initial siege and mass arrest; both were treated by the Red Crescent.

label: Marj Si — Settler Vehicle Attack (Aug 20, 2026)
sub: Settlers overturned a Palestinian vehicle between al-Mughayyir and Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah, wounding five to six people including Musa Abu Alia and Lafi Abu Naim.

label: Sa'ir — 17-Year-Old Killed by Settlers (Aug 21, 2026)
sub: Armed settlers shot and killed Karim Sanad Raja Shalaldeh, 17, at Khirbet Hamroush after Palestinians threw rocks at settlers on an 'unauthorized hike'; a 70-year-old man was also wounded and homes were reportedly torched.

label: Jenin — Fathi Khazem Killed in IDF Raid (Aug 21, 2026)
sub: Paratroopers Brigade soldiers shot and killed retired PA colonel Fathi Khazem, 58, during an overnight arrest raid on his home; IDF said he attacked a soldier with a knife.

label: Deir al-Balah — Hamas Commander Killed in Drone Strike (Aug 22, 2026)
sub: IDF drone strike killed Sharif al-Hasanat, a Hamas Deir al-Balah Battalion company commander it accused of rebuilding tunnel infrastructure; Palestinian medics reported one additional death nearby, unconfirmed.

label: Az-Zawayda — Warehouse Strike Kills 4-Year-Old (Aug 23, 2026)
sub: Israeli missiles hit a warehouse, killing 4-year-old Muhammad Abdel Salam Taha and one other, wounding 6-7; IDF said it also struck a weapons-manufacturing site nearby.

label: Maghazi Camp — Hamas Commander Ismail Abu Ful Killed (Aug 23, 2026)
sub: IDF strike killed Ismail Abu Ful, whom the military identified as commander of a Hamas arms-production site in Maghazi refugee camp.

label: Askar Camp/Nablus — 14-Year-Old Islam Ajjouri Killed (Aug 23, 2026)
sub: Israeli forces shot and killed 14-year-old Islam Ahmad Ajjouri during a raid on Askar refugee camp; camp officials said there was no confrontation justifying the shooting.

label: Al-Auja, Jordan Valley — Israeli Soldier Stabbed (Aug 23, 2026)
sub: A 16-year-old Palestinian stabbed Israeli soldier Elhanan Hananya, 24, several times; IDF launched an hours-long manhunt and arrested the suspect.

label: Deir al-Balah — Nukhba October 7 Operative Killed (Aug 24, 2026)
sub: IDF strike killed two Hamas militants, including Mohammad Abd al-Nasser Jabr Abu Asaad, a Nukhba force member who took part in the October 7, 2023 attack.

label: Sheikh Radwan, Gaza City — Mosque and Desalination Plant Struck (Aug 24, 2026)
sub: Israeli aircraft struck a mosque and a water desalination plant in the Sheikh Radwan neighborhood, per Palestinian reports; no casualty figures immediately available.

label: Beit Lahiya — Home Strike Kills 3 (Aug 25, 2026)
sub: Israeli strike on a residential building near Kamal Adwan Hospital killed three Palestinians and wounded others overnight into Aug 25.

label: Khan Younis (al-Mawasi) — Drone Strike on Civilian Gathering (Aug 25, 2026)
sub: An Israeli drone strike hit a gathering of civilians in the al-Mawasi area, killing one man and wounding three others.

label: Kafr Aqab, East Jerusalem — UNRWA Training Center Raided and Seized (Aug 25, 2026)
sub: Israeli forces raided the UNRWA-run Qalandiya Training Centre, expelled all staff, and announced plans to convert it into a municipal facility; UN Secretary-General Guterres condemned the raid.

label: Madama, West Bank — MK Sukkot Smashes Palestinian Memorial (Aug 25, 2026)
sub: Far-right MK Zvi Sukkot used a sledgehammer to destroy a memorial to Palestinians during an IDF-escorted tour; the IDF said he acted 'deceptively and manipulatively' outside the coordinated plan.

label: Shati Refugee Camp, Gaza City — Hamas Commander Killed (Aug 27, 2026)
sub: An Israeli drone strike killed Bilal Ibrahim Saleh Raqi'i, identified by the IDF as a commander in Hamas's anti-tank unit.

label: Jenin, Tulkarm & Nur al-Shams Camps — Israel Blocks Return of 33,000 Displaced (Aug 26, 2026)
sub: The Israeli government told the High Court it will keep barring the return of residents to the three refugee camps entirely cleared during Operation Iron Wall, citing intelligence that armed groups could regroup.
